title: Cryptarithmetic & Symbol Arithmetic
relevance: Tests systematic constraint reasoning under time pressure—carry logic, distinct-digit assignments, and leading-zero bans are staples of campus OAs and puzzle rounds.
company_notes: Wrapped OA variants cite eLitmus (KEY + KEY = LOCK) and Amazon (even-digit passcode ABC × D = 1728).

phases.goal: Establish the encoding rules and carry bounds that every cryptarithm must obey.

must_hit.point: Each letter represents a distinct digit from 0 to 9.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States letters are a one-to-one mapping onto digits 0–9 with no reuse.

must_hit.point: The leading digit of any number is never 0.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly bans leading zeros on every addend and the sum.

must_hit.point: Solve column by column from the right while tracking carry.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes right-to-left column processing with carry into the next column.

must_hit.point: In two-number addition the carry out is always 0 or 1 because the maximum column sum is 9 + 9 + 1 = 19.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives the 0/1 carry bound and cites max sum 9+9+1=19.

probes: What are the ground rules of a cryptarithmetic addition puzzle, including what carries are legal?

hints.1: Think about what a letter stands for and what is illegal at the start of a number.
hints.2: Mention distinct digits, the leading-zero ban, and right-to-left columns with carry.
hints.3: State: distinct digits 0–9, no leading 0, column-by-column from the right; two-addend carry is 0 or 1 since 9+9+1=19.

phases.goal: Show how carry and length bounds force letter values column by column.

must_hit.point: In SEND + MORE = MONEY, M is the carry from the thousands column, so M = 1.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Identifies the leftmost M as a carry and concludes M=1 from the max carry of 1.

must_hit.point: In EAT + THAT = APPLE, EAT + THAT ≤ 999 + 9999 = 10998 < 11000, so the 5-digit sum lies in [10000, 10998], forcing A = 1 and P = 0.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses the size bound 10998 and interval [10000, 10998] to get A=1, P=0.

must_hit.point: In GO + TO = OUT, O is the carry from the tens column so O = 1, and units O + O = T gives T = 2.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sets O=1 from hundreds carry, then 1+1=2 for T.

must_hit.point: For find-the-digit sums with known constants, compute carries from those digits first to get a simple relation such as A + B = C + 9.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains deriving A+B=C+9 (or similar) directly from fixed-digit carries.

probes: Walk through how the leftmost columns force M in SEND+MORE=MONEY and A,P in EAT+THAT=APPLE.

hints.1: Start with length or carry into the leftmost digit—not with free search over all letters.
hints.2: For MONEY, M is only a carry; for APPLE, bound the sum below 11000.
hints.3: Conclude M=1; and from 999+9999=10998, sum in [10000,10998] so A=1 and P=0.

phases.goal: Choose which column to attack first when speed matters.

must_hit.point: Under time pressure, start with the most-constrained column—usually the leftmost (dictates carries) or the rightmost (dictates parity).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names leftmost-for-carries vs rightmost-for-parity as the first-move heuristic.

must_hit.point: Constraint-satisfaction cryptarithms are graded on speed, so the first move should shrink the search space ASAP.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Links interview grading on speed to attacking the tightest constraint first.

probes: When you open a cryptarithm under a clock, do you start left or right—and why?

hints.1: Ask which column is most constrained before assigning free letters.
hints.2: Contrast leftmost carry/leading-digit force with rightmost parity/unit constraints.
hints.3: Say: start with the most-constrained column—leftmost for carries, rightmost for parity—because these CSPs are graded on speed.

phases.goal: Apply the same carry and distinct-digit discipline to OA-style and symbol-substitution variants.

must_hit.point: With K = 8 and E = 3 in KEY + KEY = LOCK, the unique valid LOCK is 1678.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recovers LOCK=1678 after rejecting the non-distinct Y=4 case.

must_hit.point: For distinct even digits with ABC × D = 1728, the solution is 864 × 2, so A+B+C+D = 20.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Picks D=2, ABC=864 (all even, distinct) and sum 20.

must_hit.point: In PQ × 3 = RQQ, Q × 3 ending in Q forces Q = 5 (Q = 0 is impossible), then P = 8 and R = 2.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Eliminates Q=0, sets Q=5, derives P=8, R=2 from 85×3=255.

must_hit.point: Under +→×, −→÷, ×→−, ÷→+, the expression 16 − 4 + 2 × 5 ÷ 3 translates and evaluates under BODMAS to 6.

probes: Given K=8 and E=3, what is LOCK in KEY+KEY=LOCK, and how do you reject invalid digit assignments?

hints.1: Double KEY and watch carries into LO, then check distinctness for Y.
hints.2: LO is 16 or 17; tens 3+3+c shows no carry to hundreds, so LO=16.
hints.3: Y=9 works: 839+839=1678 with all letters distinct; Y=4 collides O and C.

tradeoffs.topic: Leftmost column first vs rightmost column first
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Begin at the most-constrained column: leftmost usually fixes carries and leading digits; rightmost usually fixes parity or unit-digit relations. These CSPs are graded on speed, so the first move should cut the search space immediately.

tradeoffs.topic: Carry-first algebra vs blind digit search on find-the-digit sums
tradeoffs.strong_answer: When constants are already written in the columns, compute the carries they force first; that turns the letters into a short equation such as A + B = C + 9 instead of trying free assignments.

gotchas.trap: Assigning any free digit to a letter once a local column looks satisfied.
gotchas.correction: Every final assignment must satisfy the entire sum/product and keep all letters on distinct digits.

gotchas.trap: Allowing 0 on leading letters while brute-forcing (e.g. K or L in KEY + KEY = LOCK).
gotchas.correction: Skip 0 for every leading letter; K ≠ 0 and L ≠ 0 are hard constraints.
